text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert — enterprise tenant 'orchid-corp' reporting elevated 5xx rate from eu-west-1 (orchid-dedicated-eu1). Recent deploy? SLA risk: degraded API responses for tenant-specific endpoints. Pager: high-volume 502s for /v1/generate.
opsbot: Auto-check: orchid-dedicated-eu1 pool overall health = 68% healthy, avg latency 420ms, active tokens spiked x3. Warm nodes available in eu-central-1 (orchid-warm-eu2).
maria-sre: I'm taking lead. pinging @orchid-tam to confirm no customer-side changes. Starting runbook "regional-reshuffle -> tenant-traffic-shift".
ashley-eng: on standby to modify routing and update canary weights. I'll look at proxy logs (nginx/gateway) and model router traces.
jamal-sre: grabbing metrics dashboards now — spikes at 14:02 UTC, coincides with backend instance churn in eu-west-1 hostgroup. Could be upstream LB rebalancing.
orchid-tam: Orchid Systems confirming no changes on their side. They're seeing slow responses and 502s from our endpoint from their EU office. Requesting ETA.
maria-sre: Ok, plan A: shift tenant traffic to warm pool in eu-central-1 (orchid-warm-eu2) with short DNS TTL canary. Steps: 1) Spin up additional warm GPUs (opsbot shows 3 nodes ready) 2) Update regional routing layer to send 10% traffic to eu2 via internal route override 3) After 5m checks -> 50% -> 100% 4) Update public CNAME for tenant to point to eu2 edge and set TTL back to normal.
ashley-eng: I'll push route change for canary. Command (internal):
```
# route service control
rwctl routes set --tenant orchid-corp --from eu-west-1 --to eu-central-1 --weight 10 --scope temporary
```
Monitoring will be via /metrics and synthetic probes.
jamal-sre: starting canary now. Creating canary synthetic: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}" https://orchid.orchid-corp.api.redwood.com/v1/generate`
opsbot: Canary deployment started: 10% traffic -> orchid-warm-eu2. Warm pool nodes provisioned: 3.
maria-sre: @k_customer_success please inform the Orchid TAM that we're initiating a regional reshuffle; expected impact reduced as traffic moves. Keep them in the loop on propagation times (TTL 60).
k_customer_success: Notifying Orchid Systems. Sending a short message + zoom invite. Zoom: https://zoom.redwood.zoom/orchid-incident
satoshi-se: Quick note — don't change TLS termination on public CNAME; we only update CNAME target for edge. Certs are shared; certs already present at eu2 edge.
oncall-ml: checking model runtime health in eu2; KV cache will be cold initially — expect slight latency increase for first few requests. Recommend enabling prefix cache warming for their top prompts.
maria-sre: Observability: error rate on canary node = 1.2% 5xx (vs 28% on eu-west), avg latency 210ms. Good sign. Proceeding to 50% in 3m if stable.
ashley-eng: bumping to 50%. Command executed.
jamal-sre: 50% stats: 5xx down to 0.9%, p95 latency 230ms. eu-west still high.
orchid-tam: Orchid acknowledges, appreciate the canary. Asking whether we can route only critical traffic first (their prod API key).
maria-sre: We can do key-scoped routing but it requires a rule update. Given current telemetry, we'll continue weight-based shift to minimize complexity; can revisit if issues.
opsbot: Route weights updated to 50% -> eu2.
maria-sre: Preparing public DNS step: current CNAME orchid-corp.api.redwood.com -> orchid-eu1.edge.redwood.net. TTL currently 300. We'll lower authoritative TTL to 60, update CNAME to orchid-eu2.edge.redwood.net, monitor DNS propagation, then restore TTL. Any objections?
satoshi-se: No objections. Ensure the CDN edge is warmed and health-checked.
ashley-eng: lowering TTL now via DNS API: `dnsctl set-ttl orchid-corp.api.redwood.com 60`
opsbot: TTL updated to 60s.
maria-sre: Updating CNAME in 30s window to catch low TTL. Will post once done.
(30s)
maria-sre: CNAME update pushed -> orchid-eu2.edge.redwood.net.
jamal-sre: Running dig for quick verification: `dig +short orchid-corp.api.redwood.com` -> returns eu2 edge IPs for multiple resolvers.
orchid-tam: Orchid's ops team reports 200s for initial requests now. They see reduced 5xx.
oncall-ml: Observing cold-cache latency on user prompts but overall success rate > 99%. Suggest enabling KV prewarm for top 3 prompt templates (will do).
maria-sre: Increasing traffic to 100% now. Route control command: `rwctl routes set --tenant orchid-corp --to eu-central-1 --weight 100 --remove-source eu-west-1`
opsbot: Route change acknowledged. Traffic fully shifted to orchid-warm-eu2.
jamal-sre: eu-central metrics stable. 5xx ~0.1%, latency p95 240ms (within SLO).
orchid-tam: Orchid confirms normal service, thanking Redwood. Requesting incident report and timeline for postmortem.
maria-sre: Great. We'll keep DNS TTL low for 10 minutes for safety, then restore to 300. Rolling back plan: If eu2 degrades, we can revert route weights or rehydrate dedicated pool in eu-west-1.
ashley-eng: Restoring TTL to 300 in 8m.
opsbot: TTL restored to 300.
maria-sre: Marking incident as mitigated. Creating Jira ticket RW-INC-3589 to track root cause analysis and follow-ups: investigate host churn in eu-west-1, improve warm capacity auto-population, and add guidance for key-scoped routing.
satoshi-se: I'll own RCA with infra team. Tentative postmortem meeting tomorrow 15:00 UTC.
incident-bot: Incident update: incident-2248890012 status -> mitigated; severity lowered; on-call follow-up assigned to satoshi-se.
orchid-tam: Orchid appreciates quick handling. Please CC their ops lead on postmortem: ops_lead@orchid.com.
maria-sre: Noted, CCed. Closing thread when postmortem scheduled. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
